Render a bibliography as an HTML ordered list, with DOI links

Source: R/bib-core.R
bib_html_list.Rd

The single rendering routine both citation styles in this package build on: given a bibliography as parallel vectors of citation keys, already-formatted reference text and DOIs, produce an <ol> where each entry that has a DOI links to https://doi.org/<doi>, and every other entry is marked, in place, as having no DOI – rather than silently omitting the link. When a plain url is also known (often true even when no DOI is), it's rendered as a second, explicitly labeled link alongside the "no DOI" marker, rather than dropped.

Usage

bib_html_list(keys, text, doi, url = NA_character_, cited_at = NULL)

Arguments

keys

Character vector of citation keys, used as each <li>'s id (so other output, e.g. rand_link_citations() results, can link to #<key>).

text

Character vector of formatted, HTML-escaped reference text (author/title/container/year as appropriate).

doi

Character vector of DOIs, the same length as keys; NA or "" where no DOI is known.

url

Character vector of plain URLs, the same length as keys; NA or "" where none is known. Optional.

cited_at

A named list, keys matching (a subset of) keys, each value a character vector of anchor ids to backlink to. Optional.

Value

A character vector of HTML lines.

Details

Each <li> gets id = key, so in-text citations can link down to their entry with bib_cite_link(). If cited_at names one or more anchor ids per key (by convention, the ids bib_cite_link() sets), each entry also gets an "up" backlink to every one of its citing locations – so a reader can jump from the bibliography back to where a source was actually used, not just from the citation down to the source.
